Subject: Re: Unexpected p99 spikes — urgent

Rishi,

We're seeing an intermittent increase in p99 latency over the last 36 hours that is resulting in client-side timeouts for some of our critical endpoints. The attached CSV has sample request timestamps and request IDs where downstream calls failed (see rows 14-21 for a cluster around 2027-04-17T23:40Z UTC). Overall error rate hasn't climbed much, but the tail is brutal — a handful of requests jump from ~200ms to 3–5s.

This is impacting our user flows during peak. Can you escalate to your engineering leads and let us know immediate mitigations and a timeline? We're prepared to take a brief fallback (lower concurrency) on our end but need guidance.

-Helen

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: [EXTERNAL] Intermittent p99 spikes causing inference timeouts — exec attention requested

Quick triage notes (observed on a small sample of the attached IDs):
- I pulled traces for 6 request IDs in the CSV. 4/6 exhibit a queue wait of ~2.2s before the token-generation stage starts. The wait appears as a thread-block in the serving runtime (not application-level network).
- Correlated with spikes in 'pending-requests' metric on the model pool for the customer's tenant; sudden bursty arrivals cause the worker queue to exceed our internal concurrency cap and trigger backpressure.
- I see evidence of aggressive KV cache churn for identical prefixes during the same timeframe — likely cold-cache evictions under batch pressure. This increases per-request prep time.
- No obvious GC pauses in the window; node CPU is high but not saturated.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (safe, customer-facing):
1) Raise concurrency cap for NovaCloud's model pool by +20% (short canary on 2 nodes) to reduce queueing.
2) Enable prefix/KV sticky caching for their hot routes to prevent churn (config flip, non-disruptive).
3) Temporarily increase our short token-timeout threshold in the load balancer so client-side timeouts get a small extension (1s) while we stabilize.

I will run the canary for 30 minutes and report back. If the queue waits persist, we should consider transient throttling at ingress (token-bucket) or pinning to a lower-latency model variant for a short window.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-18T10:33:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: [EXTERNAL] Intermittent p99 spikes causing inference timeouts — exec attention requested

Confirmed Marcus' findings from infra perspective. Additional operational notes:
- Autoscaler made no scaling decisions during the spike window (scaling thresholds were not breached); however, our burst capacity pool was near full due to scheduled tenants sharing the same shard — this reduced headroom.
- There's a subtle race between our batching scheduler and the per-tenant concurrency cap which can lengthen per-request queuing under bursty arrival patterns. This is consistent with the approx 2s queuing we see.

Operational plan (short-term, 0–3 hours):
- Apply Marcus' canary: raise concurrency cap on two serving nodes for NovaCloud (rollback flag ready).
- Flip prefix-caching for named route "/generate/short-text" (no restart).
- Temporarily allocate one burst node from emergency pool to the tenant's shard to restore burst headroom.
- Prepare a DUMP of pending-requests every 5m to trace recurrence.

Communications: Marissa, please tell Helen we have a 30–60 minute mitigation plan and that we'll share a post-mortem. Also propose a 1-hour incident bridge if they want real-time updates.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Brooks <helen@novacloud.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@novacloud.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected p99 spikes — immediate mitigations and next steps

Helen / Tom — update from our incident work: over the weekend we reproduced the long-tail p99 spikes on your traffic pattern and confirmed the root contributor is transient queueing caused by bursty arrivals that push requests beyond the per-tenant concurrency cap and create KV-cache churn.

What we did (completed 2027-04-18):
- Canaryed a +20% concurrency cap on 2 serving nodes (30-minute canary) — observed p99 improve by ~65% in the canary window.
- Enabled prefix/KV sticky caching on your hot route — reduced prep latency for repeated prefixes.
- Allocated one emergency burst node to your shard to restore headroom.

Immediate customer-facing mitigations we request from NovaCloud (recommended, optional):
- Temporarily stagger client bursts if possible (small jitter on concurrent requests) while we roll a stable config.
- If you prefer, we can pin short-text traffic to a slightly smaller model variant for peak windows to reduce per-request compute time — we can schedule a brief maintenance for this.

Follow-up plan (48 hours):
- SRE will monitor the DUMP logs and p99 dashboard; engineering will instrument a fix for the batching/concurrency race.
- We'll share a full post-mortem with timeline, root cause, and permanent remediation.
- As a goodwill gesture we will provide a one-week credit equal to your org's average daily inference spend for the period (Mar–Apr) affected by the instability.

Would you like a 1-hour bridge this afternoon? If not, we will continue monitoring and send a written post-mortem within 48 hours.

Thanks for the patience and the detailed samples — they made triage much faster.

—Rishi
